walkthroughs.body_html:
Fill orbitals in order: 1s 2s 2p 3s 3p 4s 3d 4p. Note 4s fills before 3d.

Example: Fe (Z=26) is 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p6 3d6 4s2. Cr and Cu are exceptions: Cr is [Ar] 3d5 4s1 and Cu is [Ar] 3d10 4s1 for stability.

Each successive IE increases as e- are removed from a more positive ion. Large jumps reveal shell structure.

For Mg: jump between 2nd and 3rd IE shows the noble gas core. Across Period 3, IE generally rises but dips at Al (3p starts) and S (paired 3p e-).

Ionic = electrostatic between ions. Covalent = shared pairs. Dative = both e- from one atom (e.g. NH4+).

VSEPR predicts shape: 2 bp linear, 3 bp trigonal planar, 4 bp tetrahedral (109.5 deg), 5 bp trigonal bipyramidal, 6 bp octahedral. Lone pairs compress bond angles by ~2.5 deg each.

mcqs.q: Where is almost all the mass of an atom located?
options: In the nucleus, made up of protons and neutrons.
Mass is spread evenly throughout the entire atom including the electron shells.
Isotopes are atoms of different elements with the same mass.
Electrons contribute significantly to the mass of an atom.

mcqs.q: Why is the 4s orbital filled before the 3d orbital?
options: Because the 4s orbital has a lower energy than 3d when both are empty, so electrons fill it first.
Isotopes are atoms of different elements with the same mass.
Because d orbitals can only fill after p orbitals in the next shell.
Because the 4s shell is closer to the nucleus than the 3d shell.

mcqs.q: What is different between two isotopes of the same element?
options: They have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.
Isotopes are atoms of different elements with the same mass.
Isotopes have different numbers of electrons, which is why their mass differs.
Mass is spread evenly throughout the entire atom including the electron shells.
